Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. 

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential concerns that might be affecting your well-being. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a really valuable way for us to get a sense of how you're doing in the postpartum period.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I want you to feel safe and supported throughout our conversation. My goal is to create a space where you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll go through them one by one. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. This will help us get a better understanding of your emotional state and identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

Let's get started with the first question. Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it feels like it's been ages since I've really laughed. I just feel so tired and overwhelmed all the time, taking care of the baby and trying to keep up with everything. Sometimes I'll be watching a funny video or something, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, this should be funny," but it just doesn't feel funny to me. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to bring me joy, and it's hard for me to see the funny side of things when I'm feeling so sad and discouraged all the time. I do have moments where I feel a little better, but they're fleeting. I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? (pausing, looking down) Sorry, I'm just feeling a little emotional today... (getting choked up)
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not really. I mean, like I said, it's been hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just so worried all the time about the baby's health and safety, and that's always on my mind. It's hard for me to relax and enjoy things when I'm feeling so anxious. And when I do try to laugh or watch something funny, it just doesn't feel the same as it used to. It's like I'm just pretending to be happy, but inside, I'm still feeling really down and overwhelmed. (pausing, looking down) I guess I just feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and it's hard for me to connect with things that used to make me happy. (starting to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this...
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really discouraged and sad a lot of the time. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like everything is so overwhelming. I mean, taking care of the baby is a big job, and it's hard for me to think about doing anything else. I feel guilty when I'm not spending time with the baby, and that makes it hard for me to enjoy anything else. Even things that I used to love, like reading or taking a walk, just don't feel enjoyable to me right now. (sighing) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living my life. And that's a hard feeling to deal with. (looking down, tears welling up in my eyes) Sometimes I feel like I'm just not good enough, like I'm failing as a mom. And that makes it hard for me to look forward to anything, because I just feel so overwhelmed and unsure of myself.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah... that's me. All the time. I feel like everything is my fault, and if something goes wrong with the baby, I just beat myself up over it. I'll be like, "If only I had done this differently, or if only I had done that..." And it's hard for me to shake that feeling, even when my partner or family members try to tell me that it's not my fault. I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough, and that's a really hard feeling to live with. (sighing) Like, the other day, the baby was crying and I couldn't get her to calm down, and I just felt like such a failure. I was like, "Why can't I even do this one thing right?" And it's hard for me to not take it personally, you know? It's like, I'm the mom, and it's my job to take care of this tiny human, and if I'm not doing it right, then I'm failing. (tearfully) It's just really hard for me to be kind to myself and not blame myself for everything that goes wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping enough? Is she healthy? Is she happy? It's like, my mind is always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard for me to calm myself down. Even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I still can't shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I worry about my relationship with my partner, I worry about my own health, I worry about the future... it's just constant. (taking a deep breath) And it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm so overwhelmed with worry. It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't help it. (looking down, tears in my eyes) It's like, I'm trapped in this cycle of anxiety and worry, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing normal mom stuff, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my mind is racing and I'm thinking about all the worst-case scenarios, and I just can't calm myself down. (taking a deep breath) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear, like something is going to happen to her, or to me, or to us. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - sometimes I'll be with my partner or family members, and I'll still feel this sense of panic. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) It's like, I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? And it's exhausting, because I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. (tearfully) I just wish I could feel calm and peaceful, like I used to before the baby was born. But now, it feels like that's just a distant memory.
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing, nodding) Yes, that's a good way to put it. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I'm not sleeping well, because the baby is still waking up at night, and even when I do get to sleep, I'm always worried that she's going to wake up and need me. And during the day, it's just a constant cycle of feeding, changing, and soothing her. I love her, of course, but it's just so overwhelming. (looking down, feeling frustrated) And on top of that, I'm trying to keep up with the housework, and cooking, and laundry... it's just too much. I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (tearfully) Some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together, you know? Like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really living. And that's a hard feeling to deal with, because I feel like I should be able to handle all of this, but I just can't. (shaking my head) It's like, I'm just trying to survive, but I'm not really thriving.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, looking down) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'm lying awake, thinking about all the things that are worrying me, and feeling really unhappy and overwhelmed. (sighing) It's like, my mind is racing, and I just can't turn it off. I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just keeps me up. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested, because I'm not sleeping well. (rubbing my eyes) I'm just so tired all the time, and it's hard to function when you're not getting enough sleep. (tearfully) And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's the feeling of being unhappy and overwhelmed that's just constant. I feel like I'm just trudging through every day, trying to get by, but not really living. (shaking my head) I just wish I could feel happy and relaxed again, like I used to before the baby was born. But right now, it just feels like that's a distant memory. (pausing, looking down) And the worst part is, when I do finally get some sleep, I often wake up feeling anxious and unhappy, like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It's like, I'm never really able to relax, because I'm always waiting for something to go wrong.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes, that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just sad all the time, and I don't know how to shake it off. It's not just that I'm tired or overwhelmed, it's like I'm actually miserable. (sighing) I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a shadow of the person I used to be. I used to be happy and carefree, but now I just feel like I'm trudging through every day, trying to get by. (wiping away tears) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be happy, you know? I have a beautiful baby, and a loving partner, and a comfortable home... but none of that seems to matter when I'm feeling this way. (shaking my head) It's like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm just numb, and sad, and miserable. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And sometimes, I just feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm failing as a mom. And that feeling is just devastating. (tearfully) I just wish I could feel happy and fulfilled again, like I used to before the baby was born. But right now, it just feels like that's a distant memory, and I don't know how to get back to that place.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down my face) Yes, that's me. I cry all the time. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even always because something's wrong, it's just... (sighing) I don't know, it's like my emotions are just right on the surface all the time, and anything can set me off. (wiping away tears) I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm so overwhelmed, or because I'm feeling so guilty about something, or because I'm just so tired. (shaking my head) It's like, I'm just a cry factory, or something. (laughing through tears) I know it sounds ridiculous, but it's just... I don't know, it's like my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I don't know how to stop it. (sobbing) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and instead I'm just this emotional mess. (looking down, feeling ashamed) I feel like I'm failing, like I'm not doing this whole mom thing right. (tearfully) But at the same time, it's just... it's like, I'm so relieved to finally be feeling something, you know? Because for a while there, I was just feeling numb, and that was even scarier. (sniffling) So, I guess... I guess the crying is just a sign that I'm still in there, somewhere, and that I'm still feeling things, even if it doesn't always feel like it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head) No, I don't think that way. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through all of this, but I've never thought about hurting myself. (looking down, feeling a little relieved) I think that's one of the few things that I've been able to hold onto, you know? The thought of leaving my baby behind, or causing my loved ones pain... it's just not something that I could ever consider. (shaking my head again) No, I've just been trying to find ways to cope with all of this, and to get through each day. It's hard, but I'm trying to focus on the things that bring me joy, and to remind myself that this is all just a season, and that it will pass. (looking up, feeling a little hopeful) I just want to get through this, and to be a good mom to my baby. That's all I can think about right now.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, which are affecting her ability to cope with the demands of motherhood. She reports difficulty sleeping, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, and anxiety about her baby's health and safety, as well as her own ability to care for her child. The patient's overall presentation suggests a need for further evaluation and support to ensure her safety and well-being.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates they have not been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, stating they've 'lost their sense of humor' and it's 'hard to connect with things that used to make me happy', which aligns with the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient expresses feeling discouraged, sad, and overwhelmed, stating they don't enjoy things they used to and feel like they're just going through the motions of being a mom, which aligns with 'Hardly at all</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option, and due to the reverse scoring, this corresponds to the highest score of 3.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high frequency of anxiety and worry, describing it as 'all the time' and 'constant', with an inability to calm themselves down, even when everything is fine.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, quite a lot' option.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have been experiencing significant unhappiness and difficulty sleeping, which is consistent with the 'Yes, most of the time' option, as they mention it's a constant feeling and they're 'just trudging through every day</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong and frequent feeling of sadness and misery, with phrases such as 'that's been me a lot lately', 'I'm just sad all the time', and 'I feel like I'm actually miserable' suggesting a pervasive and intense emotional state, aligning with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>, which includes symptoms such as depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and feelings of worthlessness or guilt. The patient's <quote>persistent sadness</quote> and <quote>loss of pleasure</quote> in activities, combined with her <quote>difficulty sleeping</quote> and <quote>feelings of worthlessness and guilt</quote>, suggest a high level of distress and impairment. According to the EPDS guidelines, a score of 27 indicates a probable depression, and the patient's symptoms and concerns align with this assessment. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and treatment
2. Encourage patient to reach out to support systems, such as family and friends, for emotional support
3. Recommend <med>stress management techniques</med>, such as deep breathing and relaxation, to help manage anxiety and feelings of overwhelm
4. Support patient in developing a <med>self-care plan</med> to prioritize her own physical and emotional well-being
5. Consider referral to a <med>postpartum support group</med> for additional support and connection with other mothers who may be experiencing similar concerns
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
